blocks.text: Config-as-code fold-in (C3). Across all four domains, the strongest form of these controls is configuration / infrastructure as code in version control: the Task Card becomes a reviewable script/procedure; Execution Proof and the Audit Trail become diffable, revertable VCS history; rollback = git revert. The agent drafts and flaw-checks pre-publish; the deterministic CI + human review is the gate — never the agent's own opinion. [SRC: design/ENRICHMENTS_v1.1.md — Theme B fold-in across S2/S5]

Deterministic-gate + variance note (C4/C6). Why insist the gate is deterministic and not "ask the model if it's ok"? Because models differ in skill, carefulness, and hallucination rate depending on how they were trained — model variance / reliability (the course term; not "bias" — we do not open the fairness topic here). You evaluate a model for your task; you do not assume. A second model adversarially reviewing the first (trying to refute, not "do you agree?") is a useful model-risk mitigation — but it has cost and shares correlated blind spots, so it complements, never replaces, deterministic checks and human approval. (Taught in depth at S3 as the root of hallucination and at S5 as an output control.) [SRC: design/ENRICHMENTS_v1.1.md — Theme A LOCKED FRAMING: variance/reliability not bias; adversarial > redundant; agent≠gate]
